title: Modernizing Leadville's natural gas system
summary: Upgrading the town's energy future while preserving its mining past
body_markdown:
Nestled high in the Rocky Mountains, Leadville, Colorado, attracts visitors seeking outdoor adventure, mountain scenery and a glimpse into Colorado's rich mining history. From skiing and hiking to fishing, hunting and boating, Leadville offers an authentic mountain-town experience that has remained largely unchanged for generations.


Unlike many resort communities that have undergone rapid development, Leadville embraces and preserves its heritage. Residents take pride in the city's unique character, which reflects its key role during the expansion of the American West.


"We’re an old mining town. You really can’t paint it any other way,” said former mayor Greg Labbe. We're never going to be some modern metropolis.”


That authenticity comes with challenges, particularly when it comes to maintaining and modernizing critical infrastructure. Because of its remote location and rugged terrain, Leadville has long relied on strong community connections and resilience. The city's layout, elevation and aging infrastructure often present unique obstacles for improvement projects.


Those challenges were evident when Xcel Energy undertook a major effort to replace Leadville's natural gas distribution system. Much of the original infrastructure dated back to the 1940s and no longer met modern safety and reliability standards. The replacement required extensive planning and construction throughout the community as crews worked to modernize a system that had served residents for decades.


The completed project is expected to provide long-term benefits for Leadville residents and businesses. By replacing aging gas lines, Xcel Energy has strengthened the reliability of the natural gas system and enhanced safety for the community. The upgraded infrastructure also supports Leadville’s future growth and economic development by ensuring residents have access to the energy resources needed to support homes, businesses and public services.


"The completion of this project means Leadville will have consistent, safe and reliable natural gas service," says Labbe. "Replacing these lines assures us into the future that we will have the energy we need to prosper as a city."
